flashcard_questions.q: Roughly what proportion of American families lived below the poverty line during the 1920s boom?
How many American farmers lost their farms during the 1920s?
What yearly income was said to be the minimum for a decent standard of living in 1920s America?
What name is given to the movement of African Americans from the rural South to northern cities?
How many African Americans left the South for northern cities between 1916 and 1930?
Which year saw race riots in over 25 American cities during the 'Red Summer'?
What name was given to the laws enforcing racial segregation in the Southern states?
Which 1921 law capped immigration at about 357,000 people a year?
Which 1924 immigration law based national quotas on the 1890 census?
What total number of immigrants a year did the 1929 Immigration Act allow?
Who re-founded the Ku Klux Klan at Stone Mountain, Georgia, in 1915?
At its peak in the 1920s, how many members did the Ku Klux Klan have?
Which scandal destroyed the Klan's reputation and caused its collapse after 1925?
How many people did Attorney General Palmer's agents arrest between November 1919 and January 1920?
The Red Scare grew out of fear following the Russian Revolution of ____.

notes: 15 cards: 6 figure/statistic, 4 term-or-event to name, 2 person to significance, 2 event to date, 1 cloze. Dropped 'melting pot' and Emma Goldman as flavour; kept the four immigration acts as a date-and-effect set.
